rationale:
Issue #152 ("Incorrect interpolation") reports that when a localization string repeats a placeholder of the same type, every occurrence is filled with the first argument: Paragraph("personal.intro", interpolation: "John Doe", "Mozart") renders "John Doe" twice. The minimized production patch touches only Sources/HTMLKit/Framework/Localization/Localization.swift and replaces the global translation.replacingOccurrences(of: "%st"/"%dt"/"%do"/"%in") calls with translation.range(of:) plus replacingCharacters(in:with:), so each argument consumes only the first remaining placeholder. Both retained hunks are the identical correction applied to the two duplicated argument-substitution switches (default table and named table) in the same function region; nothing else is modified, and no API, config, or documentation is touched. The trigger is the upstream commit's own test change plus its en-GB/web.strings fixture, exercising multiple same-type placeholders ("John Doe", 31, "Mozart", 5, 21.5) through both the default-table and tableName: "web" paths, and relies only on pre-existing APIs (Paragraph, interpolation:, tableName:, renderer.render) rather than anything the fix introduced. Strict machine evidence reports build.both_versions PASS, trigger.buggy_differential reproducing both declared selectors, trigger.fixed_clean and full_suite.fixed_all_green PASS, full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers PASS, and trigger.deterministic across 3 repetitions, both before and after minimization; because the fixture is applied on both revisions and the fixed revision is fully green, the buggy failure cannot be a missing-key artifact. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and vapor-community/htmlkit#152 is the supplied allowed key.

Issue #152 ("Incorrect interpolation", body quoted in source_candidate.issue_check.linked_issues) reports that when a localization string contains multiple placeholders of the same type, every occurrence is filled with the first matching argument: Paragraph("personal.intro", interpolation: "John Doe", "Mozart") rendering "John Doe" twice. The minimized production patch touches only Sources/HTMLKit/Framework/Localization/Localization.swift and, in both duplicated interpolation switches (default-table path at ~line 130 and named-table path at ~line 203), replaces the global translation.replacingOccurrences(of: "%st"/"%dt"/"%do"/"%in") with translation.range(of:) + replacingCharacters(in:with:), i.e. first-occurrence-only substitution per argument. That is exactly the reported root cause; the two hunks are the same one-line semantic change applied to two copies of the same logic, with no refactor, rename, feature extension, doc, or config change. Traceability is fix_commit_to_merged_pr_to_issue via merged PR #153 ("Fix incorrect interpolation", single commit d9c3e10, base a142bc5 matching buggy_revision). The trigger extends two pre-existing LocalizationTests cases to pass multiple same-type arguments ("John Doe", 31, "Mozart", 5, 21.5) plus the upstream en-GB/web.strings fixture update; it uses only pre-existing public API (Paragraph, interpolation:, tableName:, renderer.render) and introduces no API added by the fix, so it is semantically equivalent to the reported defect. The fixture is applied to both revisions by trigger-tests-compatible.patch, so the buggy failure is the interpolation mismatch rather than a missing key, and this is corroborated by the strict gates: both strict_original and strict_post_minimization report passed=true with trigger.buggy_differential reproducing both declared selectors, trigger.fixed_clean, full_suite.fixed_all_green, full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, determinism over 3 repetitions, and post_minimization_validation PASS with 0 hunks removed. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and vapor-community/htmlkit#152 is the sole allowed key, so no duplicate root cause.

risks: The fix makes substitution positional and order-dependent: arguments are matched to the first remaining placeholder of their type, so a mismatch between argument order and placeholder order still yields wrong output silently.

The trigger modifies existing tests and the shared web.strings fixture rather than adding isolated ones, so the buggy revision must be run with the post-fix fixture; correctness here rests on the reported strict gates rather than an independently added test.
The Date (%dt) branch is changed by the patch but not covered by the triggering tests, which exercise only String, Int, and Double.
Placeholder tokens share a '%d' prefix (%dt vs %do); the tests do not probe whether sequential range matching can mis-target across those two tokens.
